question: Gram for gram of carbohydrate, which raises blood sugar fastest: table sugar, white bread, orange juice or an apple?
answer: White bread, at about 75 on the glycaemic index, where pure glucose scores 100; table sugar scores about 65. Starch is just glucose in chains, freed by digestion within minutes. Half of table sugar is fructose, which the liver takes up and blood glucose barely shows. Plain bread can spike faster than sweets.
move: Judge a food by what it turns into inside you, not by its name.
reference: Atkinson, F.S., Foster-Powell, K. & Brand-Miller, J.C. (2008) International tables of glycemic index and glycemic load values: 2008, Diabetes Care 31(12): 2281-2283
ask: Which of my no-sugar staples turns into glucose fastest?

items.label: Table sugar
items.note: Half of it is fructose, which raises blood glucose very little.

items.label: Apple
items.note: Fibre and cell walls slow its sugar down.

items.label: White bread
items.note: Its starch is chains of glucose that the gut snips apart within minutes.

items.label: Orange juice
items.note: The fruit's sugar without the fibre that slowed it.
